Dlugosiodlo Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Wólka Piaseczna, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in the Długosioło area is documented from 1781, and by the 1921 census the community numbered 801 — nearly half the population. All Jews were expelled from the town by German forces on October 5, 1939, the last day of Sukkot. The cemetery's own founding is undated, but likely coincided with the community's 19th-century growth; a 2010 memorial plaque near the site now commemorates roughly a thousand burials that took place here between the 18th and 20th centuries, though the cemetery itself carries no formal heritage-registry listing.
